inv_home_a_mum.text: Och, come in. The river runs right through town, and the name means mouth of the Ness. Inbhir Nis, in Gaelic.
When it is grey and wet we say dreich. When it is grey and wet and we are in a mood, crabbit. That is the whole forecast.
Flittermice come out over the Ness Islands at dusk. Stand still and they zip past your ears. Frankly, rude.

then.text: Back again? There's a pan on the hob if you want it.

else.text: Ach, a forager. I can tell by the midge bites.
Heather honey's the thing up here. Cranachan, tablet, and a thistle brooch from wool and a hawthorn pin. Wha daur meddle wi' me, and so on.
Write them down. Well, don't write the tablet down. Your dentist might read it.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. You can use my kitchen.
